mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate, as measured by FEDFUNDS, compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening phase that increases equity risk premiums, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the threshold signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in residential mortgage credit (RSAFS) signals an overheating economy that triggers aggressive monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The interaction term (UNRATE * RSAFS) fails to have a significant negative coefficient (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, characterized by high industrial production (INDPRO > 110) and strong residential mortgage credit (RSAFS > 350000), the S&P 500 experiences negative 60-day forward returns as the Federal Reserve initiates rate hikes to cool the economy.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods meeting the regime condition (INDPRO>110 and RSAFS>350000) are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE against 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000 thousand units signals weakening consumer confidence and reduced construction activity, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods with HOUST < 2000 are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the threshold signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors anticipate recession.
failure_condition: The interaction term (INDPRO * GDPC1) fails to have a significant negative coefficient (p > 0.05) in a regression of 5-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In labor market overheating regimes (UNRATE < 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 60-day forward returns due to the Federal Reserve's preemptive rate hikes to prevent inflation.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE < 4.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03.
